title: Early Christian Warning
english: For corrupt communication corrupts good character, as the all-wise Paul says.

I say that those wishing to have a steadfast mind must hold firm in correct faith, as if guarding some pearl in the mind, giving nothing at all; for they creep in, providing a place of boldness to those willing to practice superstitious religion.

For it is written: 'After a holy one, holy you will be, and with an innocent man you will be innocent, and with the chosen you will be chosen, and with the crooked you will be twisted' (Proverbs 22:11).
Julian, possessing an eloquent tongue, set it against the Savior of us all, Christ.
He also wrote three books against the holy gospels and against the wholesome religion of the Christians.
Through these he misleads many and has acted most unrighteously.
The light-minded and careless ones fall…
translator_notes: The Greek text begins mid-sentence with 'ς ἐντεθραμμένον·' and ends mid-sentence with 'πίπτου'.
baehrens: PG 76 Contra Julianum prol rem early
